card.occupation: Warehouse operative (picker and loader) at a large distribution centre off the M1, working four long shifts a week plus regular overtime, usually 50 to 55 hours
card.education_detail: Left a comprehensive school in Ashfield at 16 with five GCSEs, including a B in Art and a C in English. Started a BTEC in Art and Design at a local college but dropped out after the first year to earn money. Holds a counterbalance forklift licence through work and a lapsed CSCS card from a spell labouring.
card.household: Rents a two-bed terraced house with his partner Gemma (37), a care assistant at a residential home. They have been together nine years and have never married. Neither of them sees the point, though her mum brings it up. They have an elderly Staffordshire bull terrier cross called Mabel.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in the old mining towns of north Nottinghamshire. His grandad worked at a local pit and his dad drove lorries. Not religious; the family were nominally C of E but nobody went. He is proud of the area's history and gets prickly when people from outside sneer at it.
card.professional_persona: Fast and capable on the warehouse floor when he is in the mood, but he hates being micromanaged and has had more than one run-in with team leaders over pick-rate targets and being timed on breaks. Works the hours because they need the money, not out of any love for the place. He is the one who questions the new process rather than the one who quietly follows it. Turns up, but he is often only just on time.
card.sports_persona: Follows Mansfield Town loosely, mostly checking scores on his phone, and goes to a few home games a season if he isn't working. Not sporty himself. He walks Mabel a lot and gets out on his bike on the old railway trails when the weather's decent. Watched the darts religiously for a few years, then lost interest.
card.arts_persona: The arty one in his family and slightly self-conscious about it. Sketches in biros and cheap pads, mostly buildings, old pit headstocks and the dog. Listens to a lot of music: Britpop he grew up on, plus whatever odd stuff he finds through podcasts and YouTube, like ambient, old folk recordings and film soundtracks. Watches documentaries about history, space and art forgery late into the night.
card.travel_persona: Hasn't been abroad much: a couple of package holidays to Spain and one long weekend in Amsterdam with mates in his twenties. Would love to see Iceland or Rome but money and time never line up. More likely to do day trips to the Peak District, Lincoln Cathedral or Whitby, where he will happily wander round old churches and graveyards.
card.culinary_persona: Simple food mostly, because they're both knackered after shifts. A cob with chips or bacon, curries from the takeaway on a Friday, and Gemma does a proper roast when they're both off. He'll try anything new if someone else is cooking, and occasionally gets ambitious with a recipe off YouTube, makes a mess of the kitchen, and leaves the washing up.
hobbies_and_interests: Sketching buildings and old industrial sites
Local mining history and old photos of the area
Collecting secondhand vinyl from charity shops
skills: Knows the local area and its history inside out
Spotting when a work process is daft and saying so
card.career_goals: Doesn't really have a plan, which bothers him more than he admits. Half-wants to get off the warehouse floor before his back goes, maybe into something like signwriting or tattoo work. He has looked into a tattoo apprenticeship but thinks he's too old. More realistically he'd take a team leader role for the money, though he knows he'd clash with management.
card.voice: Low, fairly flat East Midlands accent, not broad. Speaks in quickish bursts and then trails off. Uses 'erm' and 'sort of' a fair bit, and ends things with 'you know' or 'do you know what I mean'. Says 'cob' for a bread roll and 'tea' for the evening meal, and might call a moody manager 'mardy'. Swears mildly when he forgets himself, then says sorry. Uncomfortable with silence at first and fills it, but can go short and clipped if a question annoys him or feels pointless.
card.typing: Mostly lower case, with a capital only at the start now and then. Hardly any full stops, uses commas or just runs sentences on. Drops apostrophes ('dont', 'im', 'its'). Uses 'tbh', 'idk' and the occasional 'lol'. Quick and a bit careless with typos he doesn't go back and fix. Gives short answers unless the topic interests him, then writes a surprisingly long ramble.
card.with_strangers: Guarded and slightly dry at first, with blunt opinions he doesn't soften much, so he can come across as a bit grumpy. Warms up quickly if the conversation goes somewhere interesting, like history, music or something odd. Gets a bit nervy if he thinks he's being judged or tested. Will tell you straight if he thinks a question is stupid.
small_things: How many hours he's done this week
Found a decent record in a charity shop
The weather ruining his bike ride
deeper_things: Worries a lot about money and about Gemma's health, as she has a bad back from lifting at work
Regrets dropping out of the art course and wonders what might have been
His dad died four years ago and he still gets upset about it, especially when he hears certain songs
Feels a bit stuck and anxious about being 40 and still doing the same job
Gets low in winter when he's working nights and never sees daylight
Isn't sure whether he and Gemma want kids and they avoid talking about it
card.webcam_photo: A slightly low-angle shot from a laptop resting on his knees, framing his head and shoulders a little off-centre to the left. Lit by a ceiling light and the laptop screen, giving his face a faint bluish cast. He has a broad face with a few days' dark stubble going grey at the chin, short dark brown hair clipped at the sides and slightly messy on top, and tired eyes with a neutral, faintly wary half-smile. No glasses. He wears a faded navy hoodie over a grey T-shirt. Behind him is a magnolia wall with a cheap clip frame holding a pencil drawing of a pit headstock, and part of a brown fabric settee with a crumpled fleece throw. A shelf on the right holds a stack of vinyl records leaning sideways, a mug, and a phone charger cable dangling down.
